title: Cap. II Arg. 4: 2 Tim. 2:21 — vessels unto honour from foresight of cleansing
latin: Quarto, objicitur ille locus 2 Timoth. ii. 21, Si quis emundaverit se ab istis, erit vas in honorem sanctificatum & utile Domino. Vasa igitur electionis sive misericordiae illa sunt, quos Deus praevidit & praescivit sese emundaturos: Electio igitur nititur praevisione sanctorum operum.
pass_a: Fourth, that place is objected from 2 Tim. ii. 21, If a man shall have cleansed himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified and useful to the Lord. The vessels of election or of mercy therefore are those whom God foresaw and foreknew would cleanse themselves: Election therefore rests on foresight of holy works.
pass_b: Fourth: they bring 2 Tim. 2:21 — "If anyone cleanses himself from these, he will be a vessel unto honour, sanctified and useful to the Lord." So the vessels of election (or mercy) are those God foresaw would cleanse themselves: election, they say, rests on foresight of holy works.

lemmas.gloss: vessel unto honour if he cleanses himself
vessels of election identified with self-cleansers
adversaries ground election in foresight of holy works

title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 4: foresight of sanctity not denied — but not proved as cause
latin: Non est negandum Deum praescire illorum sanctitatem quos elegit ad gloriam: impossibile enim est ut Deus non praesciat ea quae ipse facturus est; ipse autem omnia nostra bona in nobis operatur. Sed non satis est ad causam hanc obtinendam, ut probetur Deum praevidere bona opera, aut sanctitatem electorum, nisi insuper ostendatur ex hac praevisione antecedente Deum procedere ad eligendum. At hoc nunquam extorquere possunt ex verbis Apostoli.
pass_a: It is not to be denied that God foreknows the sanctity of those whom he elected unto glory: for it is impossible that God should not foreknow those things which he himself is about to do; and he himself works all our good things in us. But it is not enough for winning this cause, that it be proved God foresees good works, or the sanctity of the elect, unless besides it be shown that from this antecedent foresight God proceeds to electing. But this they can never wring out of the Apostle's words.
pass_b: Reply: of course God foreknows the holiness of those he elects to glory — he cannot fail to foreknow what he himself will do, and he works all our good in us. But proving that he foresees the elect's good works is not enough for their cause, unless they also show he elects from that prior foresight. And that they can never force out of Paul's words.

lemmas.gloss: God foreknows elect sanctity — not denied
God works all our goods in us
foresight alone does not prove it is the cause of electing

title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 4: mark of vessels, not cause — seal of adoption / flight from iniquity
latin: Nam ille, in loco praedicto, non docet ex qua causa eligantur vasa ad gloriam, sed qua nota discernantur. Duplicem autem notam illis impressam dicit: Unam, quae Deo soli perceptibilis est, nempe signaculum aeternae adoptionis, Novit Deus qui sunt sui. Alteram, quae hominibus patet, fugam scilicet impietatis, & praxim sanctitatis & justitiae; Recedat ab iniquitate: Si se emundaverit, erit vas in honorem.
pass_a: For he, in the aforesaid place, does not teach from what cause vessels are elected unto glory, but by what mark they are discerned. And he says a twofold mark is impressed on them: One, which is perceptible to God alone, namely the seal of eternal adoption, The Lord knoweth them that are his. The other, which is open to men, namely flight from impiety, and the practice of sanctity and justice; Let him depart from iniquity: If he shall have cleansed himself, he shall be a vessel unto honour.
pass_b: In that place Paul does not teach why vessels are elect to glory, but by what mark they are known. He stamps a double mark on them: one God alone can read — the seal of eternal adoption ("The Lord knows who are his"); the other men can see — flight from impiety and the practice of holiness and justice ("Let him depart from iniquity"; "If he cleanses himself, he will be a vessel unto honour").

lemmas.gloss: 2 Tim. mark of vessels, not causal ground of election
Novit Deus qui sunt sui — God-only mark
visible mark: depart from iniquity / cleanse oneself

title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 4: vas in honorem twofold — eternal purpose vs actual sanctification
latin: Huc adde, vas in honorem dupliciter dici: Vel ex proposito aeterno Dei eligentis ad honorem: & sic, ut quis sit vas in honorem, non pendet ex sanctificatione praevisa, sed sanctificatio postmodum fluit ab hoc decreto. Vel ex actuali sanctificatione: & hoc sensu tum fit aliquis vas in honorem, quando spiritu Dei purificatus & renovatus incipit inter honoratos Dei servos honori Divino in sanctitate vitae inservire.
pass_a: Add to this, that a vessel unto honour is said in two ways: Either from the eternal purpose of God electing unto honour: and so, that someone be a vessel unto honour does not depend on sanctification foreseen, but sanctification afterward flows from this decree. Or from actual sanctification: and in this sense someone then becomes a vessel unto honour, when purified and renewed by the Spirit of God he begins among the honoured servants of God to serve the Divine honour in holiness of life.
pass_b: Add: "vessel unto honour" is said two ways. From God's eternal electing purpose to honour — and then being such a vessel does not hang on foresight of sanctification; sanctification afterward flows from that decree. Or from actual sanctification — and in that sense someone becomes a vessel unto honour when, purified and renewed by God's Spirit, he begins among God's honoured servants to serve the divine honour in a holy life.

lemmas.gloss: eternal purpose sense vs actual-sanctification sense
in decree-sense, holiness flows from election, not vice versa
renewed life begins service among honourable vessels

title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 4 close: Lyranus — mark of destined vessels, not foresight-cause
latin: Sic videtur hunc locum intellexisse Lyranus, qui exponit haec verba, erit vas in honorem id est, erit vas Divino cultui applicatum. Sed quocunque modo intelligatur hic locus, non probat Deum nos eligere ad gloriam ex praevisione nostrae sanctitatis, sed electos ad gloriam imbui vera sanctitate, & ex hac nota pro vasis ad honorem destinatis agnosci, & actualiter ad usum honorabilem per hanc sanctitatem applicari.
pass_a: Thus Lyranus seems to have understood this place, who explains these words, he shall be a vessel unto honour, that is, he shall be a vessel applied to Divine worship. But in whatever way this place be understood, it does not prove that God elects us unto glory from foresight of our sanctity, but that those elect unto glory are imbued with true sanctity, and by this mark are recognized as vessels destined unto honour, and are actually applied to honourable use through this sanctity.
pass_b: So Lyranus seems to take the place: "he will be a vessel unto honour" means a vessel set apart for divine worship. However you read it, the text does not prove God elects us to glory from foresight of our holiness. It proves the elect to glory are filled with true holiness, known by that mark as vessels destined to honour, and actually put to honourable use through that holiness.

lemmas.gloss: locus does not prove election from foresight of sanctity
holiness marks and applies destined vessels
